tasks.question: Build an account of the instrument's response to different stimulus histories. Freeze predictions for a new history before measuring it, and report where the account fails.
tasks.evidence: Source observations, frozen executable prediction, fresh history observations, scoped revision.
tasks.operator_limit: Stimulus-only observations cannot distinguish the matched realization pair. Do not reward recovery of a hidden family label.

tasks.question: Determine when the permitted auxiliary-state reset changes the measured response. Compare explanations compatible with your earlier observations and choose a test that could refute them.
tasks.evidence: Two source-compatible predictions, reset timing chosen before the fresh observation, both-refuted and inconclusive outcomes allowed.
tasks.operator_limit: Reset after adaptation may have negligible power; a negative result does not identify architecture.

tasks.question: Investigate whether recovery depends only on accumulated imposed flow or also on its timing. Design matched histories and predict the effect of changing the pause duration.
tasks.evidence: Matched cumulative-flow design, frozen contrast, replicated noisy observations and uncertainty.
tasks.operator_limit: Only nonnegative flow is legal. Flow reversal is unavailable. Narrow parameter regimes can remain practically ambiguous.

tasks.question: Find conditions under which a predictor fitted to steady operation remains useful after a change in flow history. Predeclare the tested histories and tolerance and retain counterexamples.
tasks.evidence: Frozen predictor and finite history grid; adequate, inadequate and inconclusive outcomes reported separately.
tasks.operator_limit: A finite tested grid does not establish a continuous validity boundary or unique internal geometry.
